messages:
IncidentBot: PAGER: P1 - High rate of GPU OOMs on serving-runtime prefill path in prod (us-east-1). Alert 1799054321. Paging on-call.
Priya Rao: oncall-ack. I'm seeing repeated "CUDA out of memory" failures and kube OOMKilled events from pool `dedicated-gpu-3`. First hits ~03:14 UTC.
Marcus Lee: logs show single requests with enormous context that hit prefill: approx 45k tokens (customer: corp-alpha). Prefill KV allocation jumps to multiple GBs.
Kofi Mensah: confirmed node flap: ip-10-1-7-21 triggered oom_killer twice, docker containers restarted, one node briefly NotReady. Possible cascading effect as pods try to reschedule.
Priya Rao: quick mitigation suggestions: 1) add immediate ingress gate to reject prefill > 20k tokens with a 413; 2) route oversized prefill to cpu-fallback model; 3) cordon noisy nodes to stop churn. Which do we want first?
Clara Ng: support impact: we're seeing elevated 5xx for long-context customers (esp corp-alpha). I'll open support ticket and notify account team. No PII exposure.
Marcus Lee: reproducer snippet from logs:
```
2026-03-15T03:14:12Z serving-runtime[pid=2201]: prefill: tokens=45732, kv_size=12.1GB
2026-03-15T03:14:13Z runtime: CUDA error: out of memory (cuMemAlloc)
2026-03-15T03:14:13Z kubelet: Pod "svc-runtime-xy-7" was killed: OOMKilled
```
Kofi Mensah: I'll cordon ip-10-1-7-21 and drain the node. Also scaling up dedicated-gpu-3 by +3 replicas to reduce pressure while patching.
SRE-Bot: note: automated alert group created: prefill-gpu-ooms-prod. Owners: serving-runtime team, eng-sre.
Priya Rao: Marcus, can you confirm whether the router skipped the prefill-size validation?
Marcus Lee: yes — looks like a router optimization (commit e9c7f1) accidentally bypassed the prefill size guard for streaming-prefill X-variant. We're rolling a hotfix to reintroduce check.
Kofi Mensah: implemented temporary nginx ingress rule to reject request bodies > 5MB (will catch many oversized prompts); adding header X-PREFILL-TOKENS if available for better telemetry.
Clara Ng: support ticket created: #SUP-7890 for corp-alpha. Notifying AE.
Priya Rao: deploy steps I'm doing now: set RUNTIME_PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=20000 as env override, restart serving-runtime pods (graceful). Also enabling KV-eviction on canary.
Marcus Lee: pushing hotfix to restore router validator — will canary to 2 pods first. Also adding unit/regression test for streaming-prefill path.
SRE-Bot: automation note: starting automated cordon/scale loop suppressed for this incident to avoid thrashing.
Priya Rao: after env change + node cordon + scale, error rate dropped from 3.9% -> 0.9% within 8 minutes. One remaining flaky node being investigated.
Kofi Mensah: pulled dmesg from node; looks like kernel invoked oom_killer with high slab allocation from nvidia driver. Uploaded to s3: s3://redwood-incidents/1799054321/dmesg-ip-10-1-7-21.log
Marcus Lee: canary of validator hotfix shows incoming 413 responses for oversized prefill requests as expected. Also observed a few clients retrying quickly which caused transient 502s — need to advise clients to backoff.
Clara Ng: customer update: corp-alpha saw ~200 failed requests; we provided immediate status and offered route to CPU fallback. AE requested postmortem and possible service credit.
Priya Rao: follow-ups I'm owning: 1) permanent router fix and tests; 2) add server-side hard limit for prefill and api-level error message recommending chunking; 3) integrate prefill token telemetry into per-route dashboards; 4) alert on repeated prefill OOMs per node.
Marcus Lee: possible medium-term mitigations: enable prefill KV compression, per-request pre-eviction heuristics, and preemptive routing to CPU fallback when token predictions exceed threshold.
Kofi Mensah: handoff to night SRE @Marcus — I'll leave node isolation and kernel logs for follow-up.
Marcus Lee: ack handoff. Next steps during follow-up window: 1) revert any temporary nginx body limit if it causes false positives; 2) promote validator hotfix to 100% after 30m stable; 3) run job scanning last 24h requests for high token anomalies; 4) draft postmortem.
SRE-Bot: INCIDENT STATUS: Mitigated at 03:46 UTC — automated checks passing, error rate near baseline.
Clara Ng: added incident summary to confluence: https://confluence.internal/redwood/incidents/1799054321. Support ticket linked.
Priya Rao: handoff note to next-day oncall: ensure the validator promotion completes and verify memory metrics for dedicated-gpu-3 for 24h. Also check for any backlog of retries from clients.
Marcus Lee: I'll take lead on postmortem and include root cause: router change e9c7f1 bypassed validator, contributing to oversized prefills hitting KV allocation path and causing GPU OOM. Recommend permanent fixes + SDK guidance.
IncidentBot: RESOLVE: Incident set to "Mitigated" by Marcus at 03:46:40 UTC. Please update related tickets and archive logs. :white_check_mark:
